title: Kitchen Kontrol
valueStatement: AI-powered operations platform for school nutrition with inventory intelligence, forecasting, alerts, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
architectureHighlight: Turns fragmented daily tasks into actionable insights with conversational AI and real-time reporting.
description: AI-powered operations platform for school nutrition with inventory intelligence, forecasting, alerts, and human-in-the-loop workflows. Turns fragmented daily tasks into actionable insights with conversational AI and real-time reporting — offline-first, so the line still runs when the cafeteria network does not.
pitch: AI-powered operations platform for school nutrition with inventory intelligence, forecasting, alerts, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
challenge: School kitchens cannot depend on a always-on network, and paper HACCP logs were eating 30 minutes a day while still missing Texas TFER and USDA 7 CFR 210 requirements. The product had to work on wet-hands, bilingual, multi-device shifts — and still produce audit-ready evidence.
development: Shipped an interactive TypeScript/React/Vite operations demo with BroadcastChannel multi-device sync, digital HACCP logs, USDA recipe scaling, planogram builder, and an AI compliance assistant. Production roadmap layers AWS Transcribe/Lex, Bedrock, SageMaker Forecast, and Rekognition on the same workflows already proven with staff.
outcome: Reporting dropped from 30 minutes per day to 15 minutes per week; compliance rose to 95%; food waste fell to 3%. Interactive demo is a Vite app (GitHub Pages or Render — not this static portfolio). Source: github.com/rubyrayjuntos/kitchen-kontrol.

journey.title: Watch the line, not the backlog
journey.description: Observed school nutrition shifts where paper HACCP and inventory ate 30 minutes a day and still failed audits. Requirements came from wet-hands, bilingual, multi-station reality.

journey.title: Offline-first or it will not ship
journey.description: Designed the product so logging, recipes, and planograms work when the cafeteria Wi-Fi does not — then sync when a device returns.

journey.title: Make HACCP a product, not a PDF
journey.description: Turned TFER and USDA temperature rules into digital logs with signatures, pass/fail gates, and corrective-action modals staff can complete during service.

journey.title: Ops surface: planogram, recipes, inventory, meals
journey.description: Built the interactive demo hub — pan builder, USDA scaler, milk forecast, reimbursement calendar — so districts can try the workflow before a full install.

journey.title: Put AI on the same workflow
journey.description: Layered a USDA/TFER knowledge assistant, voice temperature logging, SageMaker-style demand bands, and vision checks for the line — AI that writes evidence, not a disconnected chatbot.

journey.title: Adoption is the metric
journey.description: Piloted with frontline users. Result: 15 minutes per week instead of 30 per day, 95% compliance, 3% waste, 23 school nutrition sites in the product story.

specs.title: AI compliance assistant
specs.description: In-workflow USDA/TFER assistant (Bedrock + Lambda + DynamoDB in the production design) answers food-safety questions and suggests remediation when temps are out of range — not a generic chatbot parked off to the side.

specs.title: Voice-activated HACCP logging
specs.description: Hands-free temperature and inventory capture (Transcribe, Lex, Lambda) so staff with wet or occupied hands can still produce an audit-ready log.

specs.title: ML demand forecasting
specs.description: Milk and supply forecasts from historical consumption, calendar, and confidence bands (SageMaker / Forecast / S3) instead of end-of-week guesswork.

specs.title: Vision checks on the serving line
specs.description: Photo of the line → Rekognition/Bedrock verifies pan placement and planogram alignment against the digital builder.

specs.title: Offline-first multi-device sync
specs.description: BroadcastChannel live sync between tablet and scanner viewports so the product still works when the network does not.

specs.title: Governed evidence, not screenshots
specs.description: Electronic signatures, pass/fail gates, and corrective actions mapped to Texas TFER §228.75 and USDA 7 CFR 210 — the same evidence-bound style as the rest of the AI work.
